title: The 'dot' past for -ar verbs: -é, -ó; enviar, todavía, olvidar

cards.title: The point (dot) in the past
cards.body: The 'dot' past (I spoke, I ate: finished events) is messier than the other tenses, but it has its own logic. Use hablar and comer as hooks.

cards.title: -ar dot past: hablé, habló
cards.body: Drop -ar: -é for I, -ó for he/she/it/formal you, both stressed. Careful: in this tense 'I' ends in e, not o. HAblo = I speak; haBLÓ = he spoke.

cards.title: compré, compró
cards.body: If an ending feels wrong ('comprir'), try the others; the one you've heard before will stand out.

examples.es: Me lo compró. / Lo compró para mí.

cards.title: enviar = to send
cards.body: Linked to 'envoy'. Free etymology resources (e.g. etymonline.com) are good for curiosity.

cards.title: todavía = still / yet
cards.body: Toda + vía, 'all the way'. Splitting long words into parts helps them stick.

examples.en: I haven't sent it to you yet.

cards.title: se envió = it was sent
cards.body: 'It sent itself.' Work mechanically and you won't add an unwanted lo.

examples.en: I don't know why he didn't speak with me.
examples.es: No sé por qué no habló conmigo.

cards.title: olvidar = to forget; el olvido
cards.body: El olvido is the experience of forgetting, common in songs (especially tango).

examples.en: I was going to do it, but I forgot.
examples.es: Lo iba a hacer, pero lo olvidé.
